items.title: The client deck
items.setting: Coworkers in an office after a presentation rehearsal.
items.relationship: A and B are coworkers; C is their teammate.
items.contrast: A funny mistake story versus a real work emergency.
items.cost_of_misread: If C laughs along when A is panicking, C makes the mistake feel humiliating instead of helping contain it.

version_1.label: Funny office blunder
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is offering the mistake as a ridiculous story for the group to enjoy.
version_1.correct_next_move: Join the amusement and invite the aftermath of the story.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [annoyed] I sent the client the deck with our internal comments.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [surprised] The one that says, "make this less boring"?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [big laugh] And three slides were titled, "blah."

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [laughs] Amazing. Please frame their reply when it comes in.

version_2.label: Panicked work mistake
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is nervously covering genuine fear about the consequences.
version_2.correct_next_move: Move immediately into practical support, not teasing.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [annoyed] I sent the client the deck with our internal comments.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [surprised] The one that says, "make this less boring"?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [worried] [nervous laugh] And three slides were titled, "blah."

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [worried] Okay, recall it now. I will sit with you while you call them.

items.title: The wet field
items.setting: Teammates on the sidelines after a soccer match.
items.relationship: A and B are players; C is a teammate.
items.contrast: A slapstick sports story versus a potentially serious injury.
items.cost_of_misread: If C treats an injured player like a comic act, C discourages A from getting help.

version_1.label: Slapstick fall
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is making the fall into a shared joke after the game.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [tired] I went down in front of the scouts.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [curious] On that wet patch by goal?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [big laugh] I slid all the way into the corner flag.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [laughs] That field has a personal grudge against you.

version_2.label: Scary fall
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is using a nervous laugh to avoid admitting how frightened they are.
version_2.correct_next_move: Stop the joking and get A checked out.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [tired] I went down in front of the scouts.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [curious] On that wet patch by goal?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [scared] [nervous laugh] I slid all the way into the corner flag.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [worried] Do not walk it off. Let us get the trainer and some ice.

items.title: The canceled dinner
items.setting: Three friends are already gathered at a restaurant.
items.relationship: A is dating someone; B and C are close friends.
items.contrast: A ridiculous dating anecdote versus a hurtful cancellation.
items.cost_of_misread: If C jokes about the date when A is actually hurt, A is left alone with the rejection.

version_1.label: Ridiculous excuse
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is inviting everyone to mock the melodramatic wording of the cancellation.
version_1.correct_next_move: Join the affectionate roasting of the absent date.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [tired] Devon canceled dinner thirty minutes before.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [curious] With that long voice note?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [chuckles] He called it a "plot twist."

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [laughs] A plot twist? He thinks he is television.

version_2.label: Real rejection
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is laughing nervously to keep from showing how disappointed they are.
version_2.correct_next_move: Acknowledge the hurt and make sure A is not abandoned at the table.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [tired] Devon canceled dinner thirty minutes before.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [curious] With that long voice note?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [sad] [nervous laugh] He called it a "plot twist."

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [sad] That is really disappointing. We are staying and ordering dessert with you.

items.title: The principal's office
items.relationship: A is a teenager; B and C are older cousins.
items.contrast: A mischievous school story versus a frightening disciplinary problem.
items.cost_of_misread: If C spreads a serious problem as family entertainment, A feels exposed rather than supported.

version_1.label: Mischief story
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is proudly presenting the incident as absurd family lore.
version_1.correct_next_move: Laugh with A and treat it as a story worth retelling.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [annoyed] I got called into the principal's office.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [curious] Was it for the hallway skateboard?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [laughs] Apparently the fire alarm was involved.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [big laugh] That is absolutely going in the family group chat.

version_2.label: Trouble at school
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is nervously minimizing a situation that could have real consequences.
version_2.correct_next_move: Check A’s safety and offer help dealing with the school.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [annoyed] I got called into the principal's office.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [curious] Was it for the hallway skateboard?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [worried] [nervous laugh] Apparently the fire alarm was involved.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [worried] Are you okay? Tell us what happened, and we will help you explain it.

items.title: The leaking ceiling
items.relationship: A and B are roommates; C is a friend with a spare room.
items.contrast: A bizarre housing inconvenience versus someone being overwhelmed and displaced.
items.cost_of_misread: If C makes light of the leak when A has nowhere comfortable to sleep, C ignores an immediate need.

version_1.label: Absurd apartment disaster
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is turning bad luck into a comic image.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [tired] The landlord says the ceiling leak is from upstairs.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [surprised] And it is dripping onto your bed?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [chuckles] Right onto my pillow.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [laughs] Your apartment has chosen violence.

version_2.label: Overwhelmed tenant
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is trying to laugh through a problem that has made their home unlivable.
version_2.correct_next_move: Offer immediate shelter and practical help.

turns.text: [tired] The landlord says the ceiling leak is from upstairs.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [surprised] And it is dripping onto your bed?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [sad] [nervous laugh] Right onto my pillow.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [worried] Pack a bag. You can sleep at mine, and we will take photos for the landlord.

items.title: Acting lead
items.setting: Coworkers are talking after a meeting.
items.relationship: A and B work on the same project; C is a trusted coworker.
items.contrast: A genuine career opportunity versus being pressured into unpaid extra work.
items.cost_of_misread: If C congratulates A for an exploitative arrangement, C helps normalize A being taken advantage of.

version_1.label: Exciting opportunity
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is delighted by the chance to lead, despite the imperfect offer.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [surprised] They offered me acting lead on the project.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [curious] But still no raise?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [excited] [laughs] They said it will "look great on my record."

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [delighted] Yes! That is a big step. We are celebrating after work.

version_2.label: Bitter non-promotion
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is using a bitter nervous laugh because management wants lead work for free.
version_2.correct_next_move: Name the unfairness and help A protect their boundaries.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [surprised] They offered me acting lead on the project.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [curious] But still no raise?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [annoyed] [nervous laugh] They said it will "look great on my record."

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [angry] They want lead work for free. Do not say yes until we talk about pay.

items.title: The vaccine appointment
items.setting: Friends are sitting together after a clinic visit.
items.relationship: A, B, and C are close friends.
items.contrast: A harmless embarrassing story versus lingering physical distress.
items.cost_of_misread: If C jokes while A is still scared or unwell, C may miss a need for immediate care.

version_1.label: Embarrassing recovery story
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is offering the fainting episode as a harmlessly funny memory.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [tired] I fainted during my vaccine appointment.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [surprised] Did they bring you juice?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [chuckles] I woke up holding a tiny apple juice.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [laughs] They gave you the full toddler recovery kit.

version_2.label: Still scared and dizzy
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is nervously covering that the experience still feels frightening.
version_2.correct_next_move: Check A’s condition and help them settle physically.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [tired] I fainted during my vaccine appointment.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [surprised] Did they bring you juice?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [scared] [nervous laugh] I woke up holding a tiny apple juice.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [worried] Are you still dizzy? Sit down. I will get you some water.

items.title: The great investment
items.setting: Roommates are talking in their apartment before rent is due.
items.relationship: A and B are roommates; C is a close friend who can help.
items.contrast: A self-deprecating request with room for teasing versus an ashamed financial crisis.
items.cost_of_misread: If C presses for a funny story when A is genuinely ashamed and desperate, C turns needed help into humiliation.

version_1.label: Playful money confession
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is softening a small request by inviting a little teasing about the bad purchase.
version_1.correct_next_move: Offer the help while sharing the laugh.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [worried] Could someone cover my rent until Friday?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [curious] How much are you short?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [laughs] Just eighty. I spent it on a "great investment."

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [laughs] I can cover the eighty, but I need to hear this investment story.

version_2.label: Ashamed emergency request
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is nervously trying to make a painful money problem sound small.
version_2.correct_next_move: Offer help without demanding an explanation.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [worried] Could someone cover my rent until Friday?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [curious] How much are you short?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [sad] [nervous laugh] Just eighty. I spent it on a "great investment."

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [worried] I can cover the eighty. You do not have to explain right now.

items.title: Table twelve's soup
items.setting: Restaurant staff are talking in the kitchen during a shift.
items.relationship: A and B are servers; C is the shift lead.
items.contrast: A chaotic service story versus a worker nearing a breakdown.
items.cost_of_misread: If C keeps teasing when A fears getting written up, C fails to provide backup during a stressful shift.

version_1.label: Kitchen chaos
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is enjoying the absurdity of a repeated mix-up.
version_1.correct_next_move: Tease A in the team’s playful style.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [tired] Table twelve sent back the soup three times.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [surprised] Because it was cold?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [laughs] Because I kept bringing them the wrong soup.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [laughs] You are officially banned from the soup station.

version_2.label: Service failure
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is laughing nervously because they feel overwhelmed and fear being disciplined.
version_2.correct_next_move: Take over the table and give A a break.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [tired] Table twelve sent back the soup three times.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [surprised] Because it was cold?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [worried] [nervous laugh] Because I kept bringing them the wrong soup.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [worried] Take five. I will handle table twelve and talk to the manager.

items.title: The neighbor's note
items.setting: Roommates are reading a note left outside their apartment.
items.relationship: A plays cello; B and C are roommates.
items.contrast: Affectionate teasing about noisy practice versus a criticism that genuinely hurts.
items.cost_of_misread: If C piles onto the joke when A feels rejected, C confirms the insult instead of defending them.

version_1.label: Playful music joke
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A finds the neighbor’s dramatic wording funny and invites teasing.
version_1.correct_next_move: Join the affectionate joke about A’s musical ambition.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [surprised] The neighbors left a note about my music.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [curious] The cello at midnight?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [chuckles] They called it "unforgettable."

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [laughs] Finally, your avant-garde era.

version_2.label: Hurt by the complaint
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is using a small nervous laugh to hide that the note stung.
version_2.correct_next_move: Reject the cruelty of the note and reassure A.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [surprised] The neighbors left a note about my music.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [curious] The cello at midnight?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [sad] [nervous laugh] They called it "unforgettable."

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [sad] That was a rude note. Your playing is getting better.
